issues.issue: The execution date is rendered "the a4. day of February 1995" so the commencement date cannot be read off the face of the instrument. The counterparty is also defined as "SENET" while every operative clause uses "ENET".
The illegible date matters because Section I.B measures the renewal term as "ten years from the date hereof" and Section I.A ends the initial term on a fixed calendar date.

The recital says Hybrid holds "certain transmission capacity of channel D2" without saying how much, leaving the residual D2 capacity undefined. Section XIII.M's option speaks instead of "the transmission capacity of channel D2" as a whole.

The recital frames the whole exchange as occurring "upon the issuance to the University of a license authorizing the University to relocate the D Group Station", which reads as a condition, while Section V.A makes the Commitment Fee payable at execution and Section II imposes immediate duties. A court could be asked whether the recital conditions the operative obligations.

The fixed end date of August 29, 1998 must be squared with Section I.B.1, which renews to a date measured "ten years from the date hereof" from an execution date the instrument does not legibly state.

The trailing "unless ENET provides ... at least ninety days notice" is separated from the operative renewal language by a two-limb "earlier of" construction, so it is unclear whether the notice defeats renewal or only limb (ii). Whether renewal is a single term or successive terms is also left open.

Renewal is conditioned on the University "hav[ing] filed an application for renewal of the License", yet Section VIII.B expressly permits the University to elect not to renew its license on one year's notice.

The Right of First Refusal is defined by reference to "any or all of the period from the expiration of the automatic renewal term ... through two years thereafter", leaving unclear whether it reaches offers negotiated during the term for post-term capacity. "Bona fide offer" and "exclusive right to match" are also undefined.

The period is measured from the automatic renewal term of Section I.B, but Section I.B's term itself may end early on FCC denial, so the ROFR window's start date depends on a contingency addressed elsewhere.

The notice is required "at the commencement of any negotiations", with no stated consequence for failing to give it. The trigger "desires to enter into an agreement" is a state of mind rather than an observable event.

The immediately following sentence of Section I.C requires that "[s]uch notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract", which cannot be reconciled with notice given at the commencement of negotiations.

"[T]erms or conditions that have the purpose or the effect of preventing ENET from exercising its Right of First Refusal" is open-ended; almost any term a third party demands could be said to have that effect. The provision gives no standard for measuring effect.
"[A]ny material term of such offer is subsequently changed" leaves materiality undefined, so the re-offer duty's trigger is contestable.

The scope of the applications rests on "such other changes ... as ENET believes necessary", a purely subjective standard. The PTP Link is described as running to the "Leesburg campus", a site not so named in Schedule B.

The University must either file or negotiate revisions "as the University shall reasonably require to accomplish the goals set forth in this paragraph", and those "goals" are stated only as comparative quality and reliability standards. The refund is of the Commitment Fee "less the University's reasonable costs", an unquantified deduction.

The University's duty to file the FCC Applications within thirty days sits against Section XII.A, which forbids any FCC filing unless the University has consented in advance and both parties have reviewed the document.

Replacement applications are said to become the "ECC Applications" rather than the "FCC Applications", so the defined term the section creates does not match the term used throughout. Filing timing turns on when "ENET reasonably determines to be provident".

The parallel fee-cap mechanism in Section XIII.A says ENET "shall notify" the University, whereas this section says ENET "may notify", leaving the same procedure mandatory in one place and optional in the other.

The University's duty is "best efforts" to amend applications "to meet the reasonable requirements of ENET", with the illustrative list expressly non-exhaustive. What amendments the University must pursue is therefore unbounded.
This paragraph substantially duplicates Section III.E.1, which imposes the same best-efforts modification duty in near-identical words, leaving it unclear which governs post-grant changes.

The provision terminates "this Service Agreement", a term used nowhere else in an instrument entitled Airtime Royalty Agreement. It also references best efforts "pursuant to Paragraph XII.A", while the prosecution duty is in Paragraph II.B.

The University retains the Commitment Fee here, while Section II.A.2 requires the Commitment Fee to be refunded when the parties fail to agree on the applications; the two fee outcomes must be reconciled.
Termination turns on whether "an alternative transmission source cannot be utilized by ENET", a standard with no criteria of cost or feasibility. Who decides that question is not stated.
"[C]onditions materially adverse to ENET" is undefined and left to ENET's own "sole discretion" to invoke. Materiality here has no benchmark.

"[C]onditions materially adverse to ENET" is again undefined, and the University's rescission right revives the Agreement on terms the parties did not originally set. The excusal of "ENET's obligations with respect to the STL Link and/or the PTP Link" leaves the corresponding royalty unaddressed.

The provision does not say what happens if the University "accept[s]" ENET's indemnity offer — whether the termination is thereby annulled — and leaves acceptance or rejection to the University's "reasonable discretion". The reference to "Paragraph XIIL.A" is also a broken cross-reference.

This section puts all reasonable legal and engineering costs of preparing the Agreement on ENET without limit, while Section XIII.N, which opens "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary", caps negotiation legal and engineering fees at $15,000.

The equipment obligations rest on undefined standards — "state-of-the-art equipment", "appropriate space", and a repurchase at "then-current market value of such used equipment" — and the closing date is written "ten years from the date hereon". None of these fixes a determinable outcome.

The $1.00 repurchase right on termination under Paragraph XI.A, and continued shared-equipment use for ten years, sit uneasily with Section XI.A's statement that the University may terminate "without further liability to ENET" and with the expiry-based market-value option in the same paragraph.
The receive sites are said to be "listed on Schedule A", but Schedule A is the list of representative programming networks; the receive sites are on Schedule B, as Section X.B.5 confirms.

The definition ends "begun broadcasting the D Group", an incomplete phrase that omits whether the station, ENET's programming, or University programming must be on air. The Start Date therefore has no clean trigger.

Section V.C fixes the first Royalty payment by a different trigger — the D Group Station being "constructed and ... broadcasting at ENET's wireless cable headend" — rather than by the Start Date defined here, which also requires the STL Link, PTP Link and Modification Plan.

The personnel must transmit programming "during the University Capacity", a garbled phrase mixing a capacity allocation with a time period. "Continuous feed" is then explained only by a parenthetical example.

ENET bears all operating and maintenance costs here, yet Section XIII.N obliges ENET to reimburse the University for costs the University incurs "operating and maintaining the D Group Station", leaving it unclear who operates.

The University's obligation is "best efforts" to seek whatever authority is "necessary" to meet "the reasonable requirements of ENET", with an expressly non-exhaustive list. The boundary of the duty cannot be fixed from the text.
This paragraph reproduces Section II.C.1 almost word for word, so the same modification duty appears twice with different trigger language and it is unclear which governs.

The compression trigger depends on manufacturers offering "reliable and cost-effective" equipment with "no material degradation in quality", none of which is measurable. Whether the twelve months run from the rules or from availability is also unclear.

The application is for compression "on channel D1", but Section IV allocates capacity by reference to channels D3 and D4 and to recapture rights on those channels, and channel D1 is nowhere allocated in the Agreement.

The bar on the University relocating or reconfiguring the D Group Station without ENET's consent must be squared with Section VIII.B, which lets the University return or decline to renew the license outright on one year's notice.

ENET Capacity is mistyped as "SENET Capacity", and the University's right to "recapture ... simultaneous use" of the same channels it has just granted entirely to ENET is internally obscure. How simultaneous use coexists with a grant of the "entire 6 MHz transmission capacity" is not explained.

The grant of ENET Capacity "for any legal purpose, without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information" conflicts with Section VII, which forbids ENET from transmitting programming outside a listed set without the University's prior approval.

The greater-of formula lists an unnumbered first limb and a limb "(ii)", and the per-subscriber limb does not state that twenty cents is a monthly figure. "[S]ubscriber to ENET's wireless cable service" is not defined by reference to the D Group Station at all.

The royalty is payable "[i]n consideration of the airtime to be provided hereunder", yet it is not tied to the Start Date defined in Section III.C, and Section XIII.M adds a second royalty on a different per-subscriber rate.

The bulk-billing formula reads "determined by dividing the total monthly revenues ... in said bulk billing divided by" ENET's prevailing rate, a duplicated operator that garbles the calculation. "[I]solated locations in the same facility" is also internally contradictory.

The certificate must show subscribers "served during each month of such period", but no period has been identified, and the count under Section V.B.1 is a single first-of-month snapshot rather than a monthly average. The dangling reference leaves the certificate's content uncertain.

The first payment trigger — the station "constructed and ... broadcasting at ENET's wireless cable headend" — differs from the Start Date defined in Section III.C, which additionally requires the STL Link, the PTP Link and the Modification Plan.

Records need be kept only eighteen months, yet the audit right extends to ninety days after service ends and "at any time or times", while thirty business days' notice is required before any audit. Those timing rules pull against each other within the same paragraph.
Proration presupposes a royalty that accrues daily, but Section V.B.1 computes the Royalty from a single subscriber count taken "as of the first day of the month" against a $2,500 monthly floor.

Calling the Royalty "the gross charge to ENET" while making the University responsible for any applicable taxes or fees points in two directions on who bears the tax. The scope of "taxes or fees" other than income taxes is also unbounded.

The general obligation is insurance "of the kinds customarily insured against by firms of established reputations" in "such amounts as are customarily carried", with the two specified policies introduced by "including, without limitation". The reach of the general words beyond the two enumerated policies is left open.

The permitted-programming list ends with a catch-all, "or an other programming agreed to by the University", whose reach against the enumerated categories is uncertain and which is itself mistyped. The University's "absolute right" to deny obscene programming also sits against the immediately preceding "consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

The prior-approval requirement conflicts with Section IV, which gives ENET the ENET Capacity "for any legal purpose, without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information or signal to be transmitted thereover".

The University must obtain all authorizations "required or desired" and take "all necessary steps" and "all reasonable steps" in successive sentences, mixing absolute and qualified standards. "[D]esired" has no identified point of reference.

The duty not to do anything that could cause the FCC to refuse renewal is expressly carved back only "[e]xcept as set forth in Section VIII.B", which permits surrender or non-renewal, and Section I.B.1 makes automatic renewal depend on a renewal application being filed.

This paragraph and Section XIII.A both govern disposal of the University's license on one year's notice with an ENET designation right, but XIII.A adds an ENET fee-sharing cap and different conditions, so two overlapping regimes exist for the same event.

The programming indemnity ends with "any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming" after a specific list of libel, slander, copyright and trademark claims, leaving the catch-all's reach open. The sub-clauses are also numbered "(1)" and "(ii)".
ENET indemnifies for harm from transmitted programming, yet Section VII gives the University approval rights over, and an absolute veto on, what programming is transmitted.

The Indemnifying Party's control of the defence is conditioned on a written acknowledgement "in form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party", a wholly subjective gate. Whether "promptly" notice is a condition of recovery is also unstated.
ENET covenants unqualified compliance with all laws, while the mirror covenant for the University in Section X.B.2 is qualified by "in all material respects".
"[R]easonable assurance of the funding necessary" states no amount, source or test, so the warranty cannot be measured against anything. The party is also mistyped as "EENET".
The University's compliance covenant is limited to "all material respects" whereas the mirror covenant in Section X.A.2 binds ENET without that qualifier.

The warranty that "Schedule B accurately identifies" the receive sites cannot be squared with Section III.B, which locates the receive sites on Schedule A, and with the several entries on Schedule B marked "Omitted".

The notification duty attaches to any event "which might reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach", a standard with no discernible threshold. What counts as an event that "might ... lead to" a breach is unbounded.

The cure conditions are joined by "either (a) ... or (b)", so on the literal text the University may terminate whenever a breach is uncured in thirty days even though ENET has undertaken substantive cure measures, which makes limb (b) meaningless. The parenthetical carve-out for money breaches sits inside limb (b) only.

The cure conditions are again joined disjunctively ("either is not cured ... or the University has not undertaken material or substantive measures"), so the second limb adds nothing and the two limbs give inconsistent results. "[M]aterial or substantive measures" is itself unmeasured.

Limb (3) lets ENET terminate on its own act of ceasing service, which is hard to reconcile with Section III.A, which withholds the University's equipment purchase option where ENET has exercised "its rights under Section XI.B.(2)".

Preserving the terminating party's damages claims is in tension with Sections XI.A and XI.B, which give each party a right to terminate "without further liability" to the other, and with Sections II.D and II.E, which terminate "without further liability between the parties".

The qualifier "subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld" is dropped into the middle of the sentence between the documents and the words "required to secure FCC approval", so what it modifies is unclear. The second sentence then makes University consent absolute, contradicting the reasonableness limit.

The absolute prohibition on any FCC filing without the University's advance consent cannot be squared with Section II.A.2, which requires the University to file the FCC Applications within thirty days or negotiate, and with Section II.B's duty to prosecute diligently.

The section uses "best reasonable efforts" in one sentence and "reasonable best efforts" in another, neither defined, alongside a flat duty to "fully cooperate with all reasonable requests". The differing formulations invite argument that different standards were intended.
This uncapped reimbursement duty must be read with Section XIII.N, which opens "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary" and caps legal and engineering fees at $15,000 for certain work.

The second sentence, "Subject to the foregoing provisions, the University may assign its authorization to an entity that does not agree to assume all remaining obligations", contradicts the first sentence, which permits assignment only if the assignee assumes those obligations. The words "[s]ubject to the foregoing provisions" cannot save a permission that is the opposite of what precedes it.

The same license-disposal machinery, including the ENET designation right and one year's notice, already appears in Section VIII.B, but there ENET's fee obligations are stated without the $15,000 cap set out here.

"ENET shall assist in the development of such program" states an obligation with no content, cost allocation or standard of performance. The program itself is described only as the University's "intention".

The integration clause states the entire agreement "with respect to the subject matter", yet Section XIII.Q subordinates the University's obligations to the separate Hybrid Agreement, which governs part of the same channel capacity.

The excuse extends to "other orders or requirements ... or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties" after a list of fires, strikes, embargoes and the like, leaving the catch-all's reach against the enumerated specifics open. The closing phrase "the period of dependency of any such contingency" is garbled.
The automatic extension of all time requirements sits against Section XIII.R, which makes every time for performance of the essence.

The covenant not to "take any action which would adversely affect the rights granted by it to the other party" is unlimited and could be read to override specific rights conferred elsewhere. "[B]est efforts" to execute further documents is likewise unmeasured.

The Agreement is made subject to the Communications Act, the FCC's Rules and District of Columbia law together, with no hierarchy if they diverge. Which body of law supplies the rules of construction is therefore open.

"District of Columbia courts" may mean the local D.C. courts only or any court sitting in the District, and "any party shall have the right to sue" may be permissive or exclusive. Both readings are available on the face of the clause.

Notices are deemed given on the first weekday after being sent by two named carriers only, with no rule for refusal or for notices sent by other means. The opening carve-out "[e]xcept as set forth above concerning the payment of Royalties" is not tied to a numbered section.

ENET is given an "exclusive right to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" but must exercise it within twenty-one days of a notice, so it is unclear whether the right survives non-exercise. The additional royalty formula omits any statement that the ten cents is per month.
The option over channel D2 is difficult to reconcile with Section XIII.Q, which subordinates all of ENET's rights to Hybrid's rights in channel D2 under the Hybrid Agreement.

The $15,000 cap on negotiation legal and engineering fees conflicts with Section II.F, which puts "[a]ll reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering, in connection with the preparation of this Agreement" on ENET without limit.

The trigger is a regulatory change that "would adversely affect the ability of the parties to perform", with no threshold, and the remedy is only a duty to "negotiate in good faith" — an agreement to agree. Nothing states what happens if negotiations fail.
This paragraph cites the FCC's Report and Order in MM Docket No. 93-106 as released July 9, 1994, whereas Section IV cites the same Report and Order (FCC 94-147) as released July 6, 1994.

The proviso that "no action shall be taken hereunder" if in the University's reasonable judgment it would adversely affect Hybrid gives the University a unilateral escape from any obligation, which is hard to reconcile with the Section IV capacity grant and the Section XIII.M option over channel D2.

Making every stated time of the essence pulls against Section XIII.F, which automatically extends all notice and performance periods for force majeure, and against the several "best efforts" and "as soon as reasonably possible" duties.

The clause preserves rights after an "express or implied waiver", but does not say what an implied waiver is or whether the waived breach itself remains actionable. Its reference to failures "in the future or in the past" is also confused.

The Final Order definition drives the termination triggers in Sections II.D, II.E and III.A, but Section II.E.3 sets a ten-day window running from "such event" without saying that finality is required there.
